desktop-ch10.jpg.title: Transcription ends
desktop-ch10.jpg.caption: The terminator hairpin has folded and the polymerase releases the RNA. The ribosome continues on its own.
desktop-ch10.jpg.note: couple-terminate (terminator hairpin folded at RNAP exit prior to release)

desktop-ch11.jpg.title: Stop codon
desktop-ch11.jpg.caption: Release factor RF1 reads UAA and frees the 40-residue peptide.
desktop-ch11.jpg.note: release (RF1 at UAA stop codon, hydrolysis & 40-aa peptide)

desktop-ch12.jpg.title: Finished
desktop-ch12.jpg.caption: In coupled expression, transcription and translation overlap in time and space, which is possible because bacteria have no nucleus.
desktop-ch12.jpg.note: finale (wide view: re-annealed DNA, free mRNA, ribosome, 40-aa peptide)

desktop-ch06.jpg.title: RNA emerges
desktop-ch06.jpg.caption: The 5′ end of the mRNA, with its Shine–Dalgarno sequence, leaves the polymerase while transcription continues.

desktop-ch07.jpg.title: Ribosome joins early
desktop-ch07.jpg.caption: In bacteria a ribosome can start on an mRNA that is still being made. Here transcription pauses briefly so the steps can be seen.
desktop-ch07.jpg.note: couple-scan (30S+IF1+IF3+IF2+fMet-tRNA bound at expressome, 62 nt paused)

desktop-ch08.jpg.title: 70S assembly
desktop-ch08.jpg.caption: The 50S subunit joins and the initiation factors leave. NusG links the ribosome to the polymerase, 38 nucleotides behind its active site.
desktop-ch08.jpg.note: couple-join (70S assembled, NusG bound bridging RNAP & ribosome)

desktop-ch09.jpg.title: Coupled elongation
desktop-ch09.jpg.caption: The polymerase and ribosome move together. Every three nucleotides transcribed match one codon translated.
desktop-ch09.jpg.note: couple-run (expressome moving together, coupledMrna spacer, NusG, tRNAs & peptide)
